findings.description: median calls values.sort() with no comparator, which sorts numbers lexicographically as strings, and it sorts the caller's array in place.
findings.scenario: median([10, 9, 2]) sorts to [10, 2, 9] and returns 2 instead of 9. median([1, 2, 10, 3]) is wrong too. The caller's array is also reordered, which affects any later percentile or display of the same array.

findings.description: average divides by values.length with no empty guard. The file's own comment says new users legitimately have no data.
findings.scenario: average([]) returns 0/0 = NaN, which shows as NaN in the dashboard and poisons any later arithmetic.
findings.fix: if (values.length === 0) return 0; (or null, as the dashboard expects) before the reduce.

findings.description: The setTimeout callback captures the function-scoped var i. By the time the callbacks run, the loop has finished and i === jobs.length.
findings.scenario: scheduleJobs([a, b, c], run) calls run(undefined) three times, because jobs[3] is undefined, and never runs a, b or c.
findings.fix: Use let i in the for loop, or iterate with jobs.forEach((job, i) => setTimeout(() => run(job), i * 100)).

findings.description: percentile on an empty array computes idx = -1 and returns undefined without signalling it.
findings.scenario: percentile([], 50) returns undefined, which can propagate into rendering as a missing value.
findings.fix: if (sorted.length === 0) return null; (or the dashboard's chosen empty value).
